title: The Round Window on the Yellow Map
synopsis: All six friends meet at Story House, and Sue chooses how her newly familiar cottage will appear on Amy's yellow map before returning home with Grandpa Ed.
continuity_state: Before: Amy has marked the new cottage location with a pencil dot. Sue has met all five friends separately, including Wendy in Far Meadow and Todd at Round Pond. Blue sound book, brown Button Town envelope, and garden folder remain on Story House shelf; lantern remains tilted. After: With Sue's input, Amy draws stone cottage between Doorway Tree and fenced mill on accurate real yellow map, symbolized by a round window and small yellow star representing Sue's green cushion. Amy keeps map and returns to Blue Door Cottage with Grandma. Everyone safely returns by established paths with grown-ups. Sue's cushion and castle bakery remain at Round Window Cottage; the spoon is in kitchen drawer; the blue cart remains with Grandpa. The Story House shelf remains three collections, no new project. Sue is established recurring friend without pressure to abandon memories of the previous home; season closes fully.

related_resources.reason: NAEYC's statement discusses valuing each child's perspective and opportunities for participation in a community. The specific map conversation is original fiction, not a tested strategy.
ZERO TO THREE recognizes that young children vary in reactions to change and may appreciate old familiar objects. The line represents one possible fictional experience.
